{
  "winner": "B",
  "reasons": [
    "The question asks for a paying customer within 90 days. Idea A's own seed source (dashp, via starterstory) reports about 5 months of founder time per closed deal, which already overshoots the window. The brief also notes that AI agents don't obviously shorten an in-person, trust-based sale.",
    "Idea B has a measurable, self-serve acquisition path that a solo operator with agents can run right away. Meta lead ads cost about $12.30 per lead and Google about $62–$118 CPL, both sourced. Idea A's channels are slow in-person outreach or a PestWorld booth that costs $3,475–$4,500 and is already sold out for 2026.",
    "Idea B's price anchors are sourced and live: Kickresume charges $8–24/mo and WeGoUp $9.99/mo. At those prices, a single B2C conversion is a low bar to clear within 90 days.",
    "Idea B's build is a bounded text LLM pipeline with near-zero marginal cost. Idea A has to match pest-specific incumbents like D2DHQ, whose escrow, attrition, and QuickBooks logic is already detailed, and it carries wage-law and 1099 compliance risk that is hard for an unstaffed operator.",
    "Idea A does have stronger evidence that customers pay in general (dashp at about $100k ARR, D2DHQ's published tiers). That evidence is about long-run viability, not first revenue inside 90 days, so it doesn't decide this question."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "Idea A's demand evidence does not show demand for software from the actual payer. The brief says owners pay, but both quotes describe reps' grievances against employers: a single complaint-site post about one company, and a litigated $217k commission dispute. Neither shows a pest control owner looking for or paying for commission-tracking software, and owners may have little incentive to fix opacity that a rep sues them over.",
  "confidence_note": "Moderate to low. Idea A has better evidence of real willingness to pay, through dashp's ARR and D2DHQ's pricing. Idea B faces several free competitors, has no verified free-to-paid conversion rate, and only has CPL figures rather than cost per paying customer. The pick for B rests mainly on the 90-day constraint and the sourced 5-month sales cycle in A. If 'paying customer' meant sustainable revenue rather than a first sale, A would likely win."
}
